newsitem.title: USA: J. Aron says to scale back physical cocoa business.
newsitem.headline: J. Aron says to scale back physical cocoa business.

text.p: Goldman, Sachs & Co division J. Aron & Co. said Friday it plans to scale back its physical cocoa operations internationally and denied rumours it will close its cocoa trading desk in New York.

"Goldman, Sachs will remain in the cocoa derivative business, but will de-emphasize the physical cocoa business," a company spokesman told Reuters. "We retain the option to do physical business when appropriate and justified.
"We will continue to trade cocoa as part of the GSCI (Goldman, Sachs Commodity Index) and as a part of our general commodities arbitrage business."
J. Aron declined to give any specific reason for the company's decision to de-emphasize physical cocoa operations.

No timeline was given for the change in physical operations, but the spokesman said it would be effective shortly. They also would not comment on how many people would be affected by the move or costs associated with the action.
Traders said talk J. Aron would shut down cocoa operations in New York began swirling around the industry on Thursday.
"Rumours began flying around the market yesterday," one floor trader said.
After J. Aron closed its cocoa and coffee trading desks in London about a year ago, many market sources had expected New York to follow suit.
Coming on the heels of a similar move by Cargill Inc, J. Aron's decision raised few eyebrows among commodity traders.
"It is not surprising," one trader said. "It reflects the state of affairs."
He noted compared to 10 years ago, the cocoa business has seen a consolidation in manufacturers, as well as growers.
In August, Cargill Inc. announced it was getting out of the physical cocoa business in the U.S. because it had not been able to produce a desireable return on investmemt.
-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk, 212 859 1640
